question: A connected MCP server named docs exposes a resource for the authentication guide. A developer wants to have Claude directly analyze that specific document as part of their prompt, the same way they would reference a local file. What is the correct way to do this?
options: A) Ask the agent in plain language to "open the docs server" and trust that it infers which specific resource is relevant without any reference syntax
B) Add a resources field naming the document inside .mcp.json so it loads automatically into context at the start of every session
C) Call the server's list_resources tool manually first, then paste the raw JSON result from that call directly into the next prompt
D) Type an @ mention in the prescribed form, such as @docs:file://api/authentication, to reference that exact resource inline in the prompt
correct_answers: D) Type an @ mention in the prescribed form, such as @docs:file://api/authentication, to reference that exact resource inline in the prompt
explanations: Vague natural-language requests don't reliably resolve to one specific resource; the @ mention syntax exists precisely so a specific resource can be referenced unambiguously.
There is no .mcp.json resources field for auto-loading specific documents at session start; resources are discovered from the connected server and referenced on demand via @ mentions.

Claude Code already provides tools to list and read MCP resources automatically when referenced; manually invoking a list call and pasting raw output is unnecessary and bypasses the intended @ mention workflow.
Correct. Resources are referenced with @ mentions in the form @server:protocol://resource/path, letting a developer point at a specific resource inline just like referencing a file.
